thread:
maya: Quick bench dump — ran nova13b (FP16 baseline) vs FP8/INT8 profiles on H100 and A100 across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. TL;DR: INT8 -> ~2.6x token/s on H100, ~2.4x on A100; FP8 -> ~1.5–1.7x. Small QA regressions on INT8 (~0.9 percentage points exact-match). Full csv + logs: s3://redwood-inference/quant-results/1728889999/ 

sam: Nice. Can you paste the microbench config? kernel choice, microbatch, seq len, and whether KV cache was enabled? @maya 

maya: sure — minimal snippet we used:
```
model: nova13b
precision_profile: { fp16, fp8, int8 }
kernel_hint: cutlass_fused  # default; we also tried triton_matmul_v2 for H100
microbatch: 8
seq_len: 512
kv_cache: true
warmup_iters: 40
measure_iters: 300
continuous_batching: true
streaming: true
```
We kept token generation steady (sampling seed fixed) to compare quality. Command: `./bench --model nova13b --profile int8 --gpu h100 --region us-west-2 --out results.csv`

jing: Noted an interesting thing — FP8 on H100 shows ~8–12% higher p95 vs FP16 at seq 1024 in our runs. Looks like dequant/quant overhead + kernel fallback for long sequences. Using triton_matmul_v2 reduced p95 by ~5% but lowered peak throughput ~3%. 

ravi: Capacity math (approx):
- H100 FP16: 120k tok/s per GPU (seq512, microbatch8)
- H100 FP8: 180k tok/s per GPU (~1.5x)
- H100 INT8: 310k tok/s per GPU (~2.6x)
- A100 FP16: 95k tok/s
- A100 INT8: 230k tok/s
If product needs 100 QPS with 32 tokens avg per request -> 3.2k tok/s sustained -> need 10 H100-FP16 or 11 A100-FP16; with INT8 you can serve with 2–3 GPUs (with headroom). These are raw microbench numbers, add 20% for real-workload variability.

sam: Interesting. Any quality numbers beyond the "exact-match" blip? perplexity or MMLU-ish? Also region variance? 

maya: Quick summary of evals we ran (same eval suite across regions):
- FP16 baseline: EM 41.2%, MMLU-like 67.8%, avg ppl 12.3
- INT8: EM 40.3% (-0.9 pp), MMLU 67.3% (-0.5 pp), ppl 12.5 (+1.6%)
- FP8: EM 41.0% (-0.2 pp), MMLU 67.5% (-0.3 pp), ppl 12.4 (+0.8%)
Region delta (us-west-2 vs eu-west-1) within noise (<0.2 pp) — perf differences larger than quality deltas.

arc-bot: perf-ci: nightly/quant-profiles/1728889999 -> PASS (latency regression <1% on canary, QA regression measured 0.85pp for int8). Link: https://ci.redwood/jobs/1728889999 

jing: Kernel note for rollout: prefer triage rule: if p95 increases >10% at seq>768 then force FP8 or FP16 kernel fallback for that region; otherwise allow INT8. Also add QA check on canary eval subset (50 examples) with threshold: EM drop <=1.0 pp.

maya: rollout plan: canary 5% traffic in us-west-2 with int8 profile (cutlass_fused) for 24h -> monitor token/s, p95, and canary EM; if passes, expand to 25% and run nightly full-eval; EU follow after 48h. I opened a dedicated rollout PR with config and feature flags.

sam: Thanks — can you attach the small csv with the per-kernel p50/p95 numbers? I'll add to perf dashboard. 

maya: uploaded as results_per_kernel.csv to the s3 path above. Key numbers (p50/p95 tok latency, ms per token):
H100 FP16: p50 1.05ms, p95 3.6ms
H100 INT8: p50 0.38ms, p95 4.1ms (note p95 higher due to fallback)
H100 FP8: p50 0.68ms, p95 3.8ms
A100 FP16: p50 1.3ms, p95 4.8ms
A100 INT8: p50 0.55ms, p95 5.2ms

ravi: I'll update capacity planner with these numbers and add recommended buffer and autoscale triggers. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks team — will track canary and post a follow-up summary in ~36h. :white_check_mark:
